I’ve added the small immutable traits objects. Now I’m wiring the abstract bases through them and fixing the constructor chain so `maxAge` is available before any subclass-specific state is initialized.
I caught a bad placeholder while wiring the traits object into `HungryAnimal`. I’m correcting that now so the rest-time behavior stays explicit instead of accidentally tied to the wrong field.

I’m now switching the concrete species classes over to the new trait objects. That removes the repeated constant lists from every subclass and makes the class body mostly say “this is the species identity” rather than “redeclare the entire rule set.”

I caught one behavioral mismatch while moving the predator config over: the resting time is species-specific, so it needs to live in the predator traits instead of being hardcoded in the base constructor. I’m fixing that before I touch anything else.
The trait objects are in. I’m doing a signature sweep now because moving `maxAge` through the constructor chain usually leaves a few stale super-calls behind.
